newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds remain down in the dumps.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds remain down in the dumps.

text.p: *Australian bond yields ended below the day's highs, but never looked like making a full recovery after an early sharp sell-off as events this week left the policy outlook unclear.
*Economists give a 50 pct chance of easing in Q1.
Australian bond yields ended below the day's highs, but never looked like making a full recovery after an early sharp sell-off as events this week left the monetary policy outlook unclear.
The benchmark 10-year bond yield came close to testing 7.25 percent just after the opening, having brushed 7.0 percent at the start of the week.

A strong quarterly capital expenditure report, still high wages growth through enterprise bargaining agreements and a cautiously balanced speech by RBA governor Ian Macfarlane saw bond prices and bill futures make lows for the week initially.

Addressing the Committee for the Economic Development of Australia (CEDA) on Thursday, Macfarlane said wage bargaining tensions were clouding the inflation outlook and excessive wage rises were difficult for monetary policy.
He also said that while the unemployment rate was too high, too easy a policy could cause job losses in the medium term.

Today's monthly Australian interest rates poll of 29 economists ahead of next Tuesday's RBA board meeting gave just a 10 percent chance of an easing in December after the 50 basis point cut in November. However, the survey showed a 50 percent possibility of an easing in the first quarter next year.

Meanwhile, the October balance of payments showed the seasonally adjusted current account deficit at A$1.788 billion and on the high side of expectations, although this had little impact on the market.
The widening from A$1.69 billion in the September shortfall, and despite a 1.0 percent rise in exports, was blamed on a further increase in the net income deficit to A$1.910 billion.
Economists said the data had no implications for policy, but did once again highlight the national savings problem.

The local market's weak performance saw yield spreads to other dollar bloc bonds continue this week's widening trend. Trading in U.S. Treasuries resumed in Tokyo with a firm tone after Thursday's U.S. Thanksgiving Day holiday. The U.S. faces personal spending/income in today's shortened session.
